## Motivation

- DCP MHA one-shot prefill gathers each request's cached prefix KV and interleaves it with that request's new-token KV.
- The old path built slice bounds from GPU `torch.cumsum` tensors; using GPU scalars as Python slice bounds forces a device-to-host sync: 4 syncs per request per MLA layer.
- On long cached prefixes (AgentX-style multi-turn) this stalls the host on every layer, although the same lengths are already on the host.

## Modifications

- `layers/dcp/comm.py`: build prefix and extend offsets on the host with `itertools.accumulate`; no GPU sync in the interleave.
- `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend` now takes `extend_seq_lens_cpu`; the unused device `seq_lens`, `extend_prefix_lens` and `extend_seq_lens` arguments are removed.
- Both callers updated: `forward_mha.py` (CUDA) and `forward_mha_rocm.py` (ROCm).
- New CPU test in `test_dcp_layout_unit.py`: request ordering, zero-length prefixes, padded extend rows.
- `test_dsv31_dcp8_gsm8k.py`: coverage note corrected; neither MHA extend path (one-shot, chunked-KV) is asserted to run.
- Outputs are unchanged: only where the offsets are computed moves.

## Accuracy Tests

| Test | Result |
|---|---:|
| Kimi-K3 DCP8 GSM8K, 1319 questions | 97.04% |
| DCP layout unit test (MI355X) | 18 passed |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Isolated helper remeasurement, 8x MI355X, ROCm 7.2: base `a99f105294` vs this PR at `58da40709c`.
  - Exact `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend` post-gather helper from each revision.
  - Kimi-K3 geometry: 24 MLA layers, 512-wide latent KV, 64-wide RoPE, BF16.
  - All 8 GPUs concurrently; per GPU 2 warmups, 7 measured iterations; median of the 8 per-GPU medians.
  - AgentX-like prefix lengths: recorded InferenceX workload mean (125K) and p90 (229K).

| Scenario | Batch | Cached / new tokens per request | Base | This PR | Delta | Saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AgentX-like, mean prefix | 4 | 125K / 512 | 38.11 ms | 27.27 ms | **-28.4%** | 10.84 ms |
| AgentX-like, p90 prefix | 5 | 229K / 512 | 74.92 ms | 61.15 ms | **-18.4%** | 13.77 ms |
| Shared prefix | 16 | 16K / 1K | 57.08 ms | 15.59 ms | **-72.7%** | 41.49 ms |
| Shared prefix | 48 | 64K / 1K | 297.59 ms | 170.01 ms | **-42.9%** | 127.58 ms |

- The DCP collective is common to both revisions and excluded, so these are helper-level gains, not end-to-end claims.
- Earlier end-to-end Kimi-K3 DCP8 serving A/B on the same machine:

| Metric | Base | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean TTFT | 1310 ms | 1271 ms | -3.0% |
| Output throughput | 524 tok/s | 531 tok/s | +1.3% |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.body:
## Motivation

- DCP MHA one-shot prefill gathers each request's cached prefix KV and interleaves it with that request's new-token KV.
- The old path built slice bounds from GPU `torch.cumsum` tensors; using GPU scalars as Python slice bounds forces a device-to-host sync: 4 syncs per request per MLA layer.
- On long cached prefixes (AgentX-style multi-turn) this stalls the host on every layer, although the same lengths are already on the host.

## Modifications

- `layers/dcp/comm.py`: build prefix and extend offsets on the host with `itertools.accumulate`; no GPU sync in the interleave.
- `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend` now takes `extend_seq_lens_cpu`; the unused device `seq_lens`, `extend_prefix_lens` and `extend_seq_lens` arguments are removed.
- Both callers updated: `forward_mha.py` (CUDA) and `forward_mha_rocm.py` (ROCm).
- New CPU test in `test_dcp_layout_unit.py`: request ordering, zero-length prefixes, padded extend rows.
- `test_dsv31_dcp8_gsm8k.py`: coverage note corrected; neither MHA extend path (one-shot, chunked-KV) is asserted to run.
- Outputs are unchanged: only where the offsets are computed moves.

## Accuracy Tests

+def _expected_interleave(prefix_rows, extend_rows, prefix_lens, extend_lens):
+    """Request i's prefix rows, then its extend rows; padded extend rows dropped."""
+    out, p, e = [], 0, 0

+class TestAllGatherKvCacheForMhaExtend(CustomTestCase):

run_helper.sh ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Run bench_helper.py on all 8 GPUs at once for one revision and print the median of per-GPU medians. # Usage: ./run_helper.sh set -euo pipefail source "$(dirname "$0")/env.sh" "$1" for d in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_TREE}/python" python "$(dirname "$0")/bench_helper.py" \ --device "${d}" --revision "$1" >"${OUT}/helper-gpu${d}.log" 2>&1 & done wait python - "${OUT}" <<'PY' import glob, json, statistics, sys rows = {} for f in glob.glob(f"{sys.argv[1]}/helper-gpu*.log"): line = next(l for l in open(f) if l.startswith("RESULT ")) for r in json.loads(line[7:]): rows.setdefault(r["scenario"], []).append(r["median_ms"]) for name, meds in rows.items(): print(f"{name:12s} median of {len(meds)} GPU medians: {statistics.median(meds):.2f} ms") PY ```

extend_lens_gpu, extend_kv, extend_pe, ) return all_gather_kv_cache_for_mha_extend( pool, attn, indices, prefix_lens, extend_lens, extend_kv, extend_pe, ) with
